Fuzzy search over municipality names

How often Levenshtein distance finds the right town despite typos

5,571 IBGE municipalities and 22,284 queries measured in October 2026

Summary

With up to 3 typos, the search ranks the right municipality first in 85.5% of queries

Verdict

Good for suggesting, not for correcting on its own

The right name is first in 85.5% of queries with 1 to 3 errors and in the top 5 in 94.9%. Exact text matching gets 0.4%.

Right name first85.5%exact match: 0.4%
In the top 594.9%in a list of 5 suggestions
With 1 error95.4%right name first
  • Removing accents before comparing fixes accent errors (5.0% → 0.1% misses), but the total drops to 85.0% from 85.5%.
  • Swapping two neighboring letters pushes the right name out of first place in 12.7% of 1-error queries.
  • Names of up to 6 letters are 14% of queries and 40% of the misses.

Official list

5,571 IBGE municipalities, 5,298 distinct names.

2

Queries with typos

Each name gets 0, 1, 2 and 3 random errors (accent, missing, extra, wrong or swapped letter): 22,284 queries.

3

Candidate queue

The 5,298 names are ranked by distance to the query, nearest first.

What distance is

Distance counts the edits from the query to the name, and the search ranks names by it

Levenshtein distance adds up the one-letter edits (replace, remove or insert) needed to turn the typed text into the name. Lower is closer. The search puts the name with the lowest distance first.

Query with 2 errors → São José do Rio Preto

Query with 1 error (swapped letters) → Colorado do Oeste

How to read

Swapping two neighboring letters is a single slip for whoever types, but Levenshtein distance counts two edits. That gap shows up again in the results.

Real examples from the query set; distances computed on lowercase text.

How to read

Error kinds

With 1 error, a swap pushes the right name out of first place in 12.7% of queries, 2.5x a deletion

% of 1-error queries where the right name lost first place, by error kind

transposition: 1,048 queries; deletion: 1,523 queries; accent: 461 queries; substitution: 1,291 queries; insertion: 1,248 queries.

How to read

  • Longer bar: the kind of error that most often knocks the right name out of first.
  • Transposition: swapping two neighboring letters counts as 2 Levenshtein edits.
  • Accent: on lowercase text, each missing accented letter counts as 1 edit.

Hypothesis to test

The Damerau variant, which counts a swap as 1 edit, should reduce these misses. It is a hypothesis: it was not measured here.

Removing accents

Removing accents fixes accent errors but raises misses for the other kinds: 85.0% against 85.5% overall

% misses · lowercase% misses · no accents

What changed

Without accents, accent errors almost vanish (5.0% → 0.1%). For the other kinds, misses go up: for swaps, from 12.7% to 16.4%.

Hypothesis

When people type the accent, it helps separate similar names; removing it brings more names close to the query. For: misses rise for every kind except accents. Not measured: how many extra ties appear.

Verdict

Strengths and limits

Strengths

  • Ranks the right name first in 85.5% of queries with 1 to 3 errors; exact matching gets 0.4%.
  • With 1 error, first in 95.4% and in the top 5 in 99.8%.
  • Names of 13 letters or more almost never miss (up to 0.9% misses).

Limits

  • Names of up to 6 letters are 40% of misses, with 14% of queries.
  • Swapping neighboring letters counts as 2 edits: 12.7% misses with 1 error.
  • By name alone, it cannot tell apart municipalities that share a name (9.1% of them).

Verdict: good for suggesting a list of municipalities; for correcting the query without confirmation, the first-place rate (85.5%) leaves about 1 query wrong in every 7.

How to use it today

Use the search to suggest a list of names, not to correct the query on its own

Use for
  • show the 5 nearest names as suggestions: the right one is among them in 94.9% of queries
Don't use for
  • replace the query with the first name without confirmation, or pick between same-name municipalities without the state

Why

Out of 100 queries with typos, 86 bring the right name first. In a list of 5 suggestions, 95.
